repository_selection.method: Public organization repository catalogue retrieved on the review date, followed by repository README review. Selection is representative, not a complete catalogue or a compatibility/maturity guarantee. Repository creation timestamps were not used as software release dates.

repositories.name: bsimvis
repositories.description: BSimVis is a tool to analyze similarities across a collection of binaries, based on Ghidra analyzers and the BSim (Behavioral Similarity) plugin. It provides an API and Web interface to upload large quantities of decompiled binaries and BSim feature vectors to a Kvrocks database for similarity analysis, function diffing, and family clustering.

editorial_checks: The 2011 founding is based on the project account, not the later GitHub repository creation date.
The initial prototype and the subsequent explicit public AGPL decision are distinguished.
The objects milestone is identified by year and the project announcement; no exact Git tag publication day is inferred.

The 16 October 2026 online Early Access announcement is distinguished from hack.lu 20th edition on 20–23 October. The conference presentation is part of the requested historical account, also supported by the announcement linking its hack.lu reveal trailer; no individual presentation day is invented.
Early Access is described as an evaluation milestone rather than a final production release.
CIRCL leadership is described alongside international community contributions; practical autonomy is explained through licensing, public formats and independently operated communities.
The standards initiative and published Internet-Drafts are not described as blanket IETF RFC adoption.
Core software and ecosystem repositories are not assumed to have identical licenses.
New companion tools are described as separate projects with their own architectures and release cycles.
The CIRCL meeting and acceleration account incorporates the historical clarification supplied for this appendix; it is not attributed to the Who page.
MISP-NG CEF funding, training and European community expansion are supported by CIRCL project pages; the feedback and ideas account also incorporates the supplied historical clarification.
attribution: New prose synthesizes facts from the cited sources and the existing book; no website illustrations or long quotations are reproduced.

author_supplied_clarifications.context: Historical additions requested during review of the appendix.
details: Alexandre Dulaunoy met Andras Iklody and proposed full-time work on MISP at CIRCL; this institutional support accelerated development.
MISP-NG helped extend MISP for a wider range of European users; training gathered operational feedback and ideas for the evolution of the project.
author_supplied_clarifications.date_handling: January 2013 refers to the start of Iklody as main full-time developer in the published project history. No exact date is assigned to the meeting or move to CIRCL.
